purpose: Prospectively test whether frozen SemRepair semantic-contract families predict later independently reported embodied-stack failures and their eventual repair classes.

frozen_mechanism_families.name: freshness or provenance loss
examples: cached decision detached from source identity

frozen_mechanism_families.name: effect-commit ambiguity
examples: request acknowledged but physical effect unknown
retry across irreversible action without receipt

frozen_mechanism_families.name: dependency-identity drift
examples: cached semantic decision survives source replacement

frozen_mechanism_families.name: termination/truncation/reset semantic confusion
examples: reset state leaks across episode ownership

admissibility.i0: Issue/PR/body/comments published before prediction already state the concrete root cause or essentially the same repair.
admissibility.i1: Failure is post-freeze and relevant, but prediction is too broad or mechanism evidence is insufficient.
admissibility.i2: Before independent resolution, freeze one specific mechanism family, affected semantic boundary, expected invariant violation, and repair class. No source patch from resolver may have been inspected.
admissibility.resolved_i2: Later independent maintainer/user resolution must materially match the frozen mechanism and repair class. Mere symptom disappearance is insufficient.

anti_leakage_rules: Never promote a pre-freeze issue into I2.
Never use a resolver patch or comment published before the frozen prediction.
If the issue body already names the mechanism, classify I0 even when SemRepair agrees.
Predictions are immutable after commit; corrections create a new candidate record and the old one remains.
Self-authored fixtures, forks, or controlled fault injections never count as external prospective matches.

l8_gate.target: At least two clean independently resolved I2 matches across repository-disjoint projects, plus at least one maintainer-retained external regression/integration.

l9_gate.target: At least three independently maintained projects retain/reuse the contract, verifier, native regression, or repair pattern, with external continuation beyond one-off author patches.
